items.cold_note: With 20C row (passage says it is Exp 2's 20C result): dent 0.6,1.0,1.8,3.9 rises every step; rebound 18,27,34,29 rises then falls -> D. But rows labelled 'Exp. 2' alone (-10,0,40) give rebound 18,27,29 rising every step and dent rising -> C; a student reading only the Exp. 2-labelled rows lands on C
items.readability_note: Table 1 labels the 20C, 60 kg/m3 row 'Exp. 1'. The key needs it (rebound 18,27,34,29 rises then falls; dent 0.6,1.0,1.8,3.9). A student who reads only the three rows labelled 'Exp. 2' (-10, 0, 40C) sees rebound 18,27,29 and dent 0.6,1.0,3.9, both rising at every step, which is distractor C. The passage text does say the 20C result belongs to Experiment 2, so the key is correct; the risk is in the on-screen label.
items.note: Key recomputed correct over all four temperatures. In my cold pass I listed C as defensible. Against the brief's definition (defensible from this passage), the sentence 'The 20C result is the 60 kg/m3 result of Experiment 1' puts 20C inside Experiment 2, so a careful student does not land on C. I recorded the issue as readability, not as second_defensible.

items.cold_note: Study 2 24 h 2.1, 48 h 2.4; 36 h between, monotone 0.6,1.3,2.1,2.4
items.readability_note: Same labelling issue as P3-Q4. 'Based on Study 2', but the 24-hour row the key depends on is labelled 'Study 1'. Using only the rows labelled Study 2 (6 h 0.6, 12 h 1.3, 48 h 2.4), 36 h lies between 12 and 48 h, and linear interpolation gives about 2.03C, inside distractor C (1.3 to 2.1). With the 24 h row (2.1), which the passage puts in Study 2, the answer is 2.1 to 2.4 (key A).
